findings.evidence: Out of context 'Learn more' names no subject or destination; it jumps to 'Sample information section'.
findings.after: How [product] collects design feedback [DATA NEEDED: product name]
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context): the surrounding text gives no context either.

findings.where: three hero links styled as buttons
findings.evidence: Links with in-page hrefs (#start, #demo, #learn) are drawn as filled buttons; after activation focus stays on the link because the target sections have no tabindex="-1", so keyboard and screen-reader users are not moved to the section they chose in all browsers.
findings.after: <section id="start" tabindex="-1" aria-labelledby="start-h"> so the in-page jump moves focus
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.3 Focus Order and 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (section labelled by its heading, A11-104).

findings.evidence: The capitals are in the source text (text-transform: none), so some screen readers spell 'DESIGN' or read it with shouting emphasis.
findings.after:
Design feedback tool

with text-transform: uppercase in CSS if caps are kept
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (presentation in content).

findings.evidence: Only a <main> landmark exists (no header, nav or footer), and the hero is not wrapped in a header or section, so the product label, h1 and CTAs share one undifferentiated region with the notice banner.
findings.after: <header> for the hero; move the notice into a role="note" element outside the hero

strengths: Body text 18px with 1.6 line height; button text white on #42516a passes contrast.
Focus order follows the visual order (three links, left to right).
